hints.title: Review gateway exposure
hints.detail: Check whether all exposed gateway services are expected on the LAN side. Pay particular attention to management interfaces and monitoring ports.

hints.title: Review DNS roles
hints.detail: Confirm whether the detected DNS-capable hosts are expected to serve DNS, and inspect their forwarding or recursion configuration if they appear unusual.

hints.title: Validate directory expectations
hints.detail: If Active Directory services are expected on this site, confirm the selected subnet and check whether LDAP, Kerberos, or Global Catalog ports are being filtered or hosted elsewhere.

hints.title: Restrict NFS access
hints.detail: Configure /etc/exports to limit NFS mounts to specific authorised client IPs or subnets. Consider whether NFS is still required or can be replaced with a protocol that supports authentication and encryption (e.g. SMB with signing, or SFTP).

hints.title: Enable mandatory SMB signing
hints.detail: On Windows Server: enable 'Microsoft network server: Digitally sign communications (always)' via Group Policy (Computer Configuration > Windows Settings > Security Settings > Local Policies > Security Options). On Linux/Samba: set 'server signing = mandatory' in host-6be4a0.conf and restart the service. Mandatory SMB signing prevents relay attacks where an attacker intercepts and forwards authentication exchanges.

hints.title: Secure printer access
hints.detail: Disable raw printing (port 9100/JetDirect) on printers where it is not required, or restrict it to the print server IP only. Enable authentication on printer management interfaces and keep firmware up to date.
